title: Data governance intake, prioritization, and escalation guidelines for logging redaction & retention
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Background:
Many enterprise customers are submitting non-bug requests that fall under 'data governance controls' (examples: structured logging redaction, configurable retention windows, PII handling policies, audit export formats). Currently intake is ad-hoc: support routes to Solutions Engineering, engineering triage happens case-by-case, and PMs lack a repeatable rubric for prioritizing these requests alongside feature work. This ticket defines a reproducible intake + prioritization + escalation guideline for PMs, support, and SE to ensure consistent decisions and measurable SLAs.

Goals:
- Define a clear intake form and minimum information needed to triage requests (sensitivity, legal/regulatory driver, example data flows, customer tier).
- Provide a scoring rubric for prioritization that balances compliance risk, customer revenue impact, engineering effort, and reuse potential.
- Document escalation rules for security/legal review and dedicated deployment (Private/VPC) considerations.
- Specify expected SLAs for initial response, triage outcome, and roadmap commitment.
- Provide examples and playbook items SE/support/PM can use in customer conversations.

Proposed intake fields (minimum required):
- Customer name and contact (email + company account ID)
- Description of requested control and desired user story
- Regulatory or contractual driver (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2 clause, contractual audit)
- Data types/examples that require redaction/retention handling (e.g., PII: name, ssn, custom token patterns)
- Affected product surface (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private / Console)
- Desired retention window or export frequency, if applicable
- Business impact if not delivered (revenue at risk, contract hold)
- Preferred timeline and migration constraints
- Attachments: example logs, contract snippet, compliance requirement doc

Scoring rubric (0-10 per axis, aggregate => prioritization band):
- Compliance urgency (0-10): legal/regulatory mandate or pending audit increases score.
- Customer revenue impact (0-10): MRR/ARR or pipeline at risk.
- Reuse potential (0-10): affects multiple customers or a platform-wide control.
- Estimated engineering effort (0-10; inverted where higher number = lower effort): smaller numbers represent large effort; convert so higher is more attractive.
- Security complexity (0-10): architectural risk, cryptography/KMS requirements.

Prioritization bands (example):
- Band A (aggregate >= 35): Fast-track to roadmap; propose canary + dedicated SLAs; start scoping within 2 weeks.
- Band B (22-34): Plan in next quarterly roadmap; include in backlog grooming for alignment with Optimize/Console work.
- Band C (<22): Offer workarounds, product education, and add to long-term backlog; identify automation or policy-based mitigations.

Escalation & owner model:
- Initial intake owner: Support or SE who logged the request must populate intake form in Zendesk + attach to Linear ticket under PM team.
- PM triage: PM reviews intake within SLA (see below) and assigns an initial band or requests clarification (must note missing fields).
- Security & Legal: Any request scoring Compliance urgency >= 7 must be routed to Security + Legal within 48 hours. Security adds a 'security-blocker' label if architecture changes required.
- Engineering engagement: If Band A or Security flagged, PM opens an RFC in Confluence and assigns an engineering lead for scoping within the sprint or dedicated capacity planning.

SLA expectations (customer-facing and internal):
- Acknowledgement to customer: within 2 business days of intake.
- Triage decision (band assigned or more info requested): within 10 business days.
- Security/legal initial advisory: within 48 hours of being routed.
- Roadmap commitment or clear workaround communicated: within scoring-band timeline (Band A: 2-6 weeks for scoping; Band B: next quarter planning; Band C: documented workaround within 2 weeks).

Example requests and recommended handling (concrete scenarios):
- Request: "Redact user identifiers from request logs for hosted API customers."
  Recommended: If single-customer and contract-driven => Band B/A depending on revenue; propose runtime redaction toggle + moderate effort. If cross-customer requirement => aim for platform flag and Band A.
- Request: "90-day retention limit versus default 365 days for all logs in Dedicated clusters."
  Recommended: High reuse and low complexity => Band A; prioritize as config toggle in Console.
- Request: "Provide audit export in CSV with user actions for compliance reporting."
  Recommended: Medium effort, high compliance value => route to Security, Band B with an initial export MVP.

Acceptance criteria (example for PM enforcement):
- Intake form exists in Confluence and as a templated Zendesk form; all new data-governance requests use template.
- Triage rubric documented and examples included in Confluence.
- PMs can demonstrate 3 closed requests using the rubric within the quarter.
- Security/legal routing runbook created with contact points and SLA table.

Open decisions / trade-offs to resolve in review:
- Should we require an internal revenue threshold for Band A auto-promotion (e.g., >$X ARR)? Pros: faster decisions for large customers. Cons: edge cases with sensitive customers on free tiers.
- Invert engineering-effort axis scoring or normalize all axes to common scale? Need alignment with ENG on how effort estimates are mapped.
- Should Dedicated/Private-specific work be on a different prioritization cadence (monthly planning) vs Hosted features?

Progress updates / meeting notes (ongoing):
- 2025-02-24: Kickoff with Security, Legal, SE. Agreed to prototype intake template and run rubric on five historical requests. Action: Anika to draft intake form, David to gather examples.
- 2025-02-28: Reviewed rubric with Eng Leads (ENG owners: ENG-4021). Concern: effort axis needs calibration against past epics. Action: ENG to provide historical effort translations by 2025-03-07.
- 2025-03-03: SE walked through three customer asks and validated the reuse scoring approach. Added 'deployment surface' as mandatory field.

- David: Run rubric against five historical tickets and summarize results (due 2025-03-14).
- Security: Provide official review flow and contact list (due 2025-03-10).

Customer comms language (templates):
- Acknowledgement: "Thanks for the submission. We've received the request and will review it against our governance prioritization rubric. Expect an initial reply within 2 business days."
- Clarification request example: "Can you attach a redacted sample log and indicate whether this applies to Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments? This will help us scope impact and compliance requirements."

Sign-off criteria for closing this ticket:
- Intake form published and Zendesk integration active.
- Scoring rubric documented with at least 5 calibrated examples.
- Security/Law approval path documented and tested with a mock request.

Notes: This ticket intentionally avoids defining engineering implementations (e.g., specific redaction libraries, retention enforcement mechanisms). Those will be captured in follow-up RFCs once the PM triage and banding rules decide which items proceed to engineering scoping.
